newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania central bank says banking sector in danger.
newsitem.headline: Albania central bank says banking sector in danger.

text.p: The Albanian central bank chief said on Sunday sky-high interest rates offered on the country's growing informal credit market endangered the development of Albania's fledgling commercial banking system.

"Excessively high interest rates create dishonest competition. They become a serious barrier to the further development of the banking system," Kristaq Luniku told government daily Rilindja Demokratike in an interview.

Alleged pyramid schemes promising returns of up to 50 percent a month to private investors in Europe's poorest country have channelled huge sums of money outside the formal banking sector over the past months.

Albania, which emerged from nearly half a century of hard-line communism in 1990, created a two-tier banking system in 1992 with the Bank of Albania serving as a central institution to the handful of commercial banks.

Luniku added the inefficiency of the country's banking sector had supported the growth of alleged pyramid schemes. He reiterated the central bank would step up the privatisation of banks to halt the growth of informal credit channels.
"We are interested in strategic investors who would invest in capital, services and competition," he added.
